thread:
Maya (VP Eng): Thanks for coming to the fireside — quick follow-ups from the runtime Q&A. I promised notes + clarifications here so folks can pick up action items.
Sam (Staff SWE, Runtime): Quick one — kernel rollout cadence: we expect weekly canaries starting next Tuesday, full rollout over 3 weeks if no regressions. Canary config: 1% traffic, 10% of canary window for L0 tests.
Priya (ML Eng): Can you clarify the long-context perf target? We heard p95 goal of <= 200ms for 2k tokens but need exact numbers for model families.
Maya (VP Eng): Good call. Target by model class: "small" (<= 2k): p50 30ms / p95 120ms, "medium" (2k-8k): p50 60ms / p95 250ms, "long" (>8k): p50 150ms / p95 500ms. These are now part of the perf SLAs for Hosted and Dedicated.
Carlos (Infra Lead): Rollout note: kernel v3 uses different CUDA kernels; we'll schedule node reboots during canary windows. Ops-bot will post drain/deploy when canary starts.
ops-bot: Canary job created: canary-id=canary-211234, start=2026-04-07T15:00:00Z, traffic=1%.
Jana (SRE): For observability, add these to per-route dashboards: kernel version tag, batch size distribution, queue length. Also want a health alert if p95 > target for 3 consecutive 1m windows.
Sam (Staff SWE, Runtime): On batching: default dynamic batching threshold will move from 8->12 tokens for text-gen to improve throughput. We will expose a per-model override flag in the model config: `max_batch_tokens` and `batch_timeout_ms`.
Priya (ML Eng): How does this interact with prefix/KV caching? Will larger batches hurt cold-start long-context queries?
Sam (Staff SWE, Runtime): Good question. We plan to prioritize requests with cache hits in routing. Cold-starts get isolated lane with lower batching to keep latency bounded. Cache TTLs: default 10m for small prefixes, 60m for session-affine caches. We'll publish recommendation table soon.
Zoe (Product): Can we get short guidance for customers on quantization tradeoffs? Customers keep asking whether to use 4-bit for latency vs quality.
Maya (VP Eng): Action item: Priya + Sam to draft a one-pager: "quantization by workload" with empirical p50/p95 and sample prompts. Target EOD Friday.
Carlos (Infra Lead): Also flag: Dedicated customers can opt into a conservative rollout (no auto-quantization) via tenant config.
Jana (SRE): Canary rollback criteria suggestion: +5% p95 relative to baseline OR +3% error rate OR any new OOM. If triggered auto-rollback + notify oncall.
Sam (Staff SWE, Runtime): We'll add a canary smoke that runs these quick evals: perf, 100 sample prompts for quality drift, and memory pressure checks.
Maya (VP Eng): One more: region routing — we will prefer local region for latency, but fallback to nearest region w/ capacity. That policy will be documented in routing.md.
Zoe (Product): Can we communicate expected user impact during canary windows in the console? Even minimal UI: "Canary in progress — small % of requests".
Carlos (Infra Lead): Yes, Console team will add banner and telem tag for affected requests.
Priya (ML Eng): Last question: kernel feature flags — will customers see kernel variant names?
Sam (Staff SWE, Runtime): We'll expose "kernel_variant" metadata in traces and logs (e.g., `kv-optimized-v3-a`) but not surface it in public API responses.
Maya (VP Eng): OK everyone — summary + action items: (1) Sam/Priya one-pager on quant/TTL (EOD Fri), (2) Sam to add `max_batch_tokens` config and publish default table (next week), (3) Jana to codify canary rollback rules (PR by Tuesday), (4) Console to add canary banner (design spike this week). I'll follow up with calendar invites. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
Sam (Staff SWE, Runtime): noted, I'll ping here when the PRs are up.
Carlos (Infra Lead): I'll coordinate node maintenance windows with infra-schedule.
Zoe (Product): I'll draft a short customer note for the changelog once we lock the wording.
Priya (ML Eng): leaving a link to a quick perf script we use for p95 measurements:
```
python perf_check.py --model gpt-open-8k --n 200 --concurrency 5
# outputs p50/p95/mean
```
Maya (VP Eng): Perfect. If anything else pops up, drop it here and we'll triage. Closing thread for follow-ups but will reopen if action items move. :sparkles:
